thread:
incident-bot: PROD ALERT — multiple model-serving pods in us-west-2 are crashlooping with SIGSEGV. Paging @devon (oncall).
devon: I'm on it. Seeing repeated SIGSEGV in runtime_engine.so in pod inference-prod-rlm-abc-7f9d. Stack shows native crash in fused kernel path.
```
[pid 12345] runtime_engine.so(+0x1a3f2) [0x7f2e1a3f2]
#0  0x7f2e1a3f2 in tensorrt_llm::fused_attention()
#1  0x7f2e1b2a1 in vllm::forward()
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
sara: Confirmed on metrics: node i-0abcd1234 flapping (kubelet restarts), dmesg shows CUDA: GPU kernel failure/CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION on the same times. Also seeing occasional OOM for long seqs.
infra-bot: Auto-detected node instability: i-0abcd1234 has >5 kubelet restarts in 10m, suggested action: cordon + drain.
mike: Propose immediate mitigations: 1) cordon node, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) scale down replicas for affected model to 0, 4) update routing policy to force fallback_model: ml-small-cpu.
devon: Running drain + scale now. Commands:
```
kubectl cordon i-0abcd1234
kubectl drain i-0abcd1234 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl scale deploy inference-prod-rlm --replicas=0 -n prod
# set routing to fallback via console API (policy id: rp-934)
```
alex: We have a tested runtime image that disables fused kernels: runtime:edge-2026-03-12 (sha: sha256:aa11). Rolling that should avoid the fused path bugs. But note: warmup time ~10-15m.
sara: Rolling will take time. Alternative short-term: change routing to cpu-quantized variant (latency up, stable) so customer-facing traffic is less likely to hit GPU fused-kernel path.
lee: Customer impact: CS reports increased 5xx for several tenants. Priority accounts affected: Acme Inc, Finlytics. CS @customer-success — can you notify them with an interim update and ETA?
customer-success: Pinged both. Acme requested an incident note. They asked: how long to full restore?
devon: Short-term plan executed: cordon/drain done, routing changed to fallback_model, scaling applied. Midterm: start rolling runtime -> runtime:edge-2026-03-12, if that doesn't clear segfaults we'll rollback to runtime:v2.4.1 (stable) and disable kernel-fusion flag.
incident-bot: Action logged: rollback/patch started by devon at 1847501305. Incident channel created: #incident-1847501234.
infra-bot: kubectl drain output:
```
Evicting pod inference-prod-rlm-abc-7f9d... evicted
Evicting pod metrics-exporter... evicted
Warning: pod inference-prod-rlm-xyz remains in CrashLoopBackOff and cannot be evicted
```
mike: If rollback doesn't stop segfaults, plan B: migrate traffic to hosted fallback fleet (hosted-redwood) and enable SLA failover for affected tenants.
devon: Rolling runtime image on daemonset now:
```
kubectl set image ds/runtime-engine runtime-engine=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:edge-2026-03-12 -n prod
kubectl rollout status ds/runtime-engine -n prod --watch
```
devon: Rollout progressing: 4/5 pods updated. One pod still CrashLoopBackOff but error changed to OOM rather than SIGSEGV. Increasing memory limit for that deployment from 8Gi -> 12Gi as emergency mitigation.
sara: Good call. Nodes stabilized — no new CUDA kernel errors in the last 3 minutes. 5xx rate down ~90% from peak. I'll keep 5m checks and watch GPU driver logs.
lee: CS notified Acme & Finlytics with interim details and that failover was applied. They requested follow-up postmortem and timeline; CS will prepare a customer note.
devon: Handing incident to night oncall @mike for follow-up for next 2h. Preliminary root cause hypothesis: fused-kernel execution path in runtime-engine (vLLM/TensorRT integration) coupled with specific NVIDIA driver/hardware combo and long sequence lengths. Reproducer work item created in infra-ml backlog.
mike: ACK, I've documented timeline and TODOs in the incident doc. Moving to monitoring phase. Please add any remaining logs or reproducer snippets to the doc. Closing active page — will escalate if regression appears.
